summary: Paul Copp is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at UMass Amherst and earned his PhD at Princeton under Stephen F. Teiser. He has held positions at Heidelberg, Western Michigan University, and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura. Attested in 2010, he served as a professor at Simon Fraser University.

Paul David Numrich specializes in religious and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate from the University of Michigan by 1992. In 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He directed Hōbōgirin (~1929–1979) and held the Chair of Chinese Language and Literature at Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn under Christian Lassen and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a professor at the University of Kiel from circa 1889 to 1919.
Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and later served there as a professor from circa 1976 to 2017.

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University (~1883–1920).
Paul Fuller is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Paul Dundas and completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Rupert Gethin.

Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Columbia University, he served in library and academic roles at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Yale University. He served as a professor of religious studies at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2010).

Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned doctorates and habilitation at Berlin and Bonn. He held professorships at the Mithila Research Institute (1954), University of Bonn (1955), and University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned his PhD at ANU under J.W. de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He taught at Canterbury and Auckland before joining Stanford University around 2006.

Paul J. Griffiths is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from UW–Madison. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (~1990–1999), UIC (2000–2007), and Duke University (~2007–2018).
Paul Kingsbury is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona, attested in 2002.

Paul L. Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his PhD at UW–Madison under Minoru Kiyota. From circa 1986 to 2021, he served as a professor at Nanzan University and directed its institute.

Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He held academic posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1973–2006) and the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Mus (1902–1969) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. He studied under Sylvain Lévi, Jean Przyluski, and Paul Pelliot, later serving at EPHE (1937), Collège de France (1946), and Yale University (~1950–1969).
Paul Nietupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held an academic post at John Carroll University, attested in 2008.

Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) was a French scholar of Sinology, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies who studied under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EFEO (1901) and Collège de France (1909, 1911–1945), and belonged to the Institut de France.

Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1870–1876) and later served at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.
